CFItems.fullStatement: Reading
Foundational Skills
Understand the role of phonological awareness in literacy development
Explains the importance of phonological awareness as a foundational skill for literacy development
Identifies and provides examples of phonemes, syllables, onsets and rimes
Identifies and provides examples of blending, segmenting, substituting, and deleting phonemes, syllables, onsets and rimes
Understands the role of phonics and word analysis in literacy development
Explains the importance of phonics and word analysis in literacy development
Distinguishes among common letter-sound correspondences and spelling conventions
Distinguishes high-frequency sight words from decodable words appropriate for particular grades
Identifies roots and affixes to decode unfamiliar words
Recognizes various stages of language acquisition (e.g., WIDA taxonomy)
Delineates common phonics and word-recognition approaches for ELLs (pedagogy)
Differentiates syllabication patterns (e.g., open, closed, CVe)
Understands the role of fluency in literacy development
Defines fluency and related terms (e.g., accuracy, rate, prosody)
Explains the impact of fluency on comprehension
Literature and Informational Texts
Understands how to use key ideas and details to comprehend literature and information text
Identifies the key details, moral, and/or theme of a literary text, citing specific textual evidence
Identifies the key details and/or central idea of an informational text, citing specific textual evidence
Makes inferences from a text and supports them with appropriate evidence
Summarizes information from a text
Analyzes the characters, setting, and plot of a literary text.
Analyzes the relationships among individuals, events, ideas, and concepts in an informational text.
Understands how features and structures of text across genres affect comprehension.
Uses text features (e.g., headers, sidebars, hyperlinks) to locate information in a print or digital informational text
Identifies organizational structures of informational text (e.g., case/effect, problem/solution)
Identifies how structural elements contribute to the development of a literary text as a whole.
Identifies structural elements of literature across genres (e.g., casts of characters and stage directions in drama, rhyme and meter in poetry)
Understands the concept of point of view using evidence from the text
Compares multiple accounts of the same event or topic to identify similarities or differences in point of view
Identifies how point of view impacts the overall structure of a literary or informational text.
Identifies author's point of view in various genres and supports conclusions with evidence from the text
Understands how to integrate and compare written, visual, and oral information from texts and multimedia sources
Compares two or more literary texts that address the same topic
Compares two or more literary texts that address the same theme
Compares two or more informational texts that address the same topic
Interprets visual and multimedia elements in literary and informational texts
Evaluates key claims in a text and supports them with reasons and evidence from the text
Explains how visual and oral elements enhance the meaning and effect of a literary text (e.g., picture book, graphic novel, multimedia presentation of a folk tale)
Knows the role of text complexity in reading development
Identifies features of text-leveling systems
Explains the three factors (i.e., quantitative, qualitative, and reader and task) that measure text complexity
Writing, Speaking, and Listening
Writing
Understand the characteristics of common types of writing
Distinguish among common types of writing (e.g., opinion/argument, informative/explanation, narrative)
Identifies the purpose, key components, and subgenres (e.g., speeches, advertisements, narrative poems) of each type of writing
Evaluates the effectiveness of writing samples of each type
Understands the characteristics of effective writing
Evaluates the development, organization, or style of a piece of writing
Identifies appropriate revisions to strengthen a piece of writing
Evaluates the appropriateness of a particular piece of writing for a specific task, purpose, and audience
Writes clearly and coherently
Identifies the interrelationships among planning, revising, and editing in the process of writing
Knows the developmental stages of writing (e.g., picture, scribble)
Identifies the grade-appropriate continuum of student writing
Knows the importance of digital tools for producing and publishing writing and for interacting with others
Identifies the purposes of a variety of digital tools for interacting with others
Identifies the characteristics and purposes of a variety of digital tools for producing and publishing writing
Knows the research process
Distinguishes between primary and secondary sources and their uses
Distinguishes between reliable and unreliable sources
Identifies the steps in the research process
Distinguishes between paraphrasing and plagiarizing
Knows how to locate credible print and digital sources, locate information within the sources, and cite the sources
Language
Knows the conventions of standard English grammar, usage, mechanics, and spelling when writing, speaking, reading, and listening
Explains the function of different parts of speech
Corrects errors in usage, mechanics, and spelling
Identifies examples of different sentence types (e.g., simple, compound, compound-complex)
Identify how varieties of English (e.g., dialects, registers) used in stories, dramas, or poems support the overall meaning
Understands how to determine the meaning of words and phrases
Identifies types of figurative language
Interprets figurative language
Analyzes the relationship between word choice and tone of a text
Determines the literal meaning of unknown words and phrases from context, syntax, and/or knowledge of roots and affixes
Understands how to determine the meaning of words and phrases
Identifies relevant features of language such as word choice, order, and punctuation
Differentiates among the three tiers of vocabulary
Speaking and Listening
Knows the characteristics of engaging oral presentations
Identifies elements of engaging oral presentations (e.g., volume, articulation, awareness of audience)
Identifies the characteristics of active listening
Knows the characteristics of effective collaboration to promote comprehension
Identifies techniques to communicate for a variety of purposes and diverse audiences
